r-0048.title_es: Ordenanza de vivienda Ban the Box de Newark (Newark Ban the Box)
r-0048.requirement_es: Los arrendadores y corredores solo pueden verificar antecedentes penales después de una solicitud formal, con aviso y consentimiento, y solo pueden revisar 8 años atrás para condenas por delitos mayores (indictable) o 5 años para infracciones de personas desordenadas (disorderly persons) (más delitos graves enumerados y cargos pendientes). No pueden usarse arrestos sin condena, registros eliminados (expunged) ni de menores, y las denegaciones requieren razones por escrito.
r-0048.key_value_es: Preguntas sobre antecedentes penales solo después de una solicitud formal; revisión de 8 años / 5 años; multas de hasta $500 la primera vez, $1,000 por reincidencia

r-0049.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7)
r-0049.requirement: Any Boston landlord ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the notice to quit or notice of non-renewal, and send a copy of the notice to the city. Fines can reach $300 per day.
r-0049.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with every notice to quit or non-renewal
r-0049.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or occupancy in Boston
r-0049.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities
r-0049.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.
r-0049.interaction: Notice-of-rights rule (the category covers notice); it does not limit the grounds for eviction, and Massachusetts has no just-cause statute. Effective 2020-11-06 per the city FAQ (D014).
r-0049.title_es: Housing Stability Notification Act (City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7)
r-0049.requirement_es: Todo arrendador de Boston que ponga fin a un arrendamiento debe entregar al inquilino un Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources (aviso de derechos y recursos de los inquilinos) junto con el aviso de desocupación o de no renovación, y enviar una copia del aviso a la ciudad. Las multas pueden llegar a $300 por día.
r-0049.key_value_es: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources con cada aviso de desocupación o de no renovación

r-0051.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Department of Neighborhood Development)
r-0051.requirement: Housing providers with city (DND) funding or land, or with income-restricted inclusionary units, may not deny everyone with a criminal record and must decide case by case. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records or convictions over 5 years old, and may not deny based on credit score.

r-0051.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
r-0051.quoted_span: Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies
r-0051.title_es: Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy de Boston (Department of Neighborhood Development)
r-0051.requirement_es: Los proveedores de vivienda con fondos o terrenos de la ciudad (DND), o con unidades inclusionarias de ingresos restringidos, no pueden denegar a todas las personas con antecedentes penales y deben decidir caso por caso. No pueden considerar arrestos sin condena, condenas selladas o eliminadas, registros de menores ni condenas de más de 5 años, y no pueden denegar con base en el puntaje de crédito.
r-0051.key_value_es: Sin prohibición general por antecedentes penales; se ignoran arrestos sin condena, registros sellados y de menores, y condenas de más de 5 años

r-0052.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single units

no_rule.note: San Diego's tenant protection division has no rent cap, and the notice it requires landlords to give (S.D.M.C. 98.0705) sends tenants to state Civ. Code 1947.12 for rent limits, while it says 'Local law also provides' only for just cause. X027 (LASSD FAQ) repeats this notice. So state 1947.12 governs San Diego rents.

D039 is a 2024-09-03 council motion that only asks LAHD to report on feasibility of a ban. The Morgan Lewis survey of local algorithmic rent laws dated 2026-08-21 (X018) lists San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley and Santa Ana but not Los Angeles, and the brief's examples omit LA. State Bus. & Prof. Code 16729 still applies.

The brief's illustrative San Francisco lookup cites only Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 for the screening fee while layering local rules in the rent, just cause and algorithmic rows; no supplied SF doc (D078 to D083) names a local fee rule. Medium confidence: no SF text positively says there is none.

Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction statute: c.186 s.12 (D051) lets either party end a tenancy at will by written notice without cause; c.186 s.11 and s.31 (D050, D058) are notice-to-quit rules for nonpayment and s.18 (D053) is anti-retaliation, none limits the grounds for eviction.

M.G.L. c.40P s.4 bars local rent control; H.3744 (D011, 193rd General Court), a home-rule petition to let Boston adopt rent stabilization, never passed (accompanied a study order 9/9/2024); IP 25-21 struck (T5).
Deposits are governed by state law M.G.L. c.186 s.15B (D052); no Boston deposit ordinance in the Boston sources (D010 to D014). Inferred, not stated by a Boston document.
M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b) (D052) limits all upfront charges statewide and c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (D057) governs broker fees; no Boston fee ordinance in D010 to D014. Inferred.
No Boston algorithmic rent-setting ordinance in any source; the only Massachusetts measures are the pending state bills S.2983 and H.5222 (D046, D045). Inferred.
M.G.L. c.40P s.4 bars local rent control in Cambridge; IP 25-21 struck (T5), so no rent cap.
Deposits governed by state law M.G.L. c.186 s.15B (D052); no Cambridge deposit ordinance in D029 or D031. Inferred.
Upfront charges limited statewide by M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b) (D052), broker fees by c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (D057); no Cambridge fee ordinance in D029 or D031. Inferred.

Cambridge Day (X026, supplied link D030) reports only a council policy order asking the city manager to draft policy options or ordinance language; no ordinance enacted or filed. State bills S.2983/H.5222 pending.
DCA Truth in Renting guide: 'The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.' Rent control is municipal (Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark records).

Organizer test T2 and the brief: the Hoboken and Jersey City bans apply only in their own cities, 'neither for Newark'; no Newark ordinance in X004 to X006. Statewide FAIR Act (NJ-06) covers Newark from 2027-07-01.
